q: What is the chemical formula of water?
explanation: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

q: Which city is the capital of France?
explanation: Paris is the capital and largest city of France.

q: How many days are there in a week?
explanation: A week has seven days.

q: Which planet of the Solar System is called the Red Planet?
explanation: Mars looks reddish because of iron oxides on its surface.

q: Who was the first human in space?
explanation: Yuri Gagarin made the first human spaceflight on 12 April 1961.

q: Who wrote the play «Romeo and Juliet»?
explanation: «Romeo and Juliet» is a tragedy by William Shakespeare.

q: Which artist painted the «Mona Lisa»?
explanation: The «Mona Lisa» was painted by Leonardo da Vinci in the early 16th century.

q: How many strings does a classical guitar have?
explanation: A classical guitar has six strings.

q: What is the name of Disney's famous mouse in red shorts?
explanation: Mickey Mouse is the best-known character of Walt Disney's studio.

q: How many players of one team are on the pitch in football (soccer) at once, goalkeeper included?
explanation: Each football team fields 11 players at a time.

q: What is cheese made from?
explanation: Cheese is made from milk that is curdled and drained of whey.

q: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
explanation: The heart works as a pump that pushes blood through the vessels.

q: Which device is mainly used to type text into a computer?
explanation: The keyboard is the main device for entering text.

q: Which language is the official language of Brazil?
explanation: Brazil speaks Portuguese, a legacy of its colonial history.

q: What do we call a person whose job is to put out fires?
explanation: Firefighters put out fires and rescue people.

q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of the planet's surface.

q: How many legs does a spider have?
explanation: Spiders have eight legs, which sets them apart from insects.

q: Which traffic-light colour means «stop»?
explanation: A red light forbids moving on.

q: In which country are the pyramids of Giza?
explanation: The pyramids of Giza stand near Cairo, in Egypt.

q: Which fairy-tale heroine lost a glass slipper at the ball?
explanation: Cinderella lost her slipper, and the prince found her by it.

q: On which instrument will you find black and white keys?
explanation: The piano has black and white keys.

q: Which sport is played with a racket and a shuttlecock?
explanation: Badminton is played with rackets and a shuttlecock.

q: Which fruit, according to legend, fell on Isaac Newton's head?
explanation: Legend says a falling apple inspired Newton's thoughts on gravity.

q: How many teeth does an adult have, wisdom teeth included?
explanation: A full set of permanent teeth is 32.

q: Which star is the closest to Earth?
explanation: The closest star to Earth is our Sun.

q: On which continent is Egypt?
explanation: Egypt lies in the north-east of Africa.

q: What is the worldwide network that connects computers called?
explanation: The Internet connects billions of devices around the world.

q: Which animal is traditionally called the «king of beasts»?
explanation: The lion is traditionally called the king of beasts.

q: Which holiday is celebrated on 1 January in many countries?
explanation: 1 January is the first day of the calendar year.

q: Which colour do you get by mixing blue and yellow paint?
explanation: Mixing blue and yellow paint gives green.

q: Which gas do people need to breathe to live?
explanation: The body needs oxygen to breathe.

q: Which city is the capital of Japan?
explanation: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

q: In which city is the Colosseum?
explanation: The Colosseum is an ancient amphitheatre in the centre of Rome.

q: Who is the author of the Harry Potter books?
explanation: The Harry Potter series was written by J. K. Rowling.

q: Which painter, according to the famous story, cut off part of his own ear?
explanation: Van Gogh injured his ear in 1888.

q: Which composer wrote the «Moonlight Sonata»?
explanation: The «Moonlight Sonata» is a work by Beethoven.

q: In which 1997 film did Leonardo DiCaprio star aboard a huge ill-fated liner?
explanation: In Titanic DiCaprio played Jack Dawson.

q: How many rings are there on the Olympic flag?
explanation: Five interlocked rings symbolise the union of five parts of the world.

q: Which plant's beans is chocolate made from?
explanation: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.

q: Which vitamin does the body make in the skin under sunlight?
explanation: Vitamin D is made in the skin when it is exposed to sunlight.

q: Which company makes the iPhone?
explanation: The iPhone is made by Apple.

q: Which language is the main official language of Spain?
explanation: Spain's official language is Spanish (Castilian).

q: What is the international organisation headquartered in New York that unites almost all countries called?
explanation: The United Nations was founded in 1945.

q: How many planets are there in the Solar System?
explanation: The Solar System has eight planets.

q: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
explanation: Russia is the largest country by area.

q: Who was the first president of the United States?
explanation: George Washington held office in 1789–1797.

q: How many hours are there in a day?
explanation: A day has twenty-four hours.

q: Who wrote the novel «Crime and Punishment»?
explanation: The novel was published in 1866.

q: In which city is the Louvre museum?
explanation: The Louvre is the great art museum of Paris.

q: How many basic notes are there in an octave (do, re, mi…)?
explanation: Do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, si — seven basic notes.

q: What is the name of the green ogre hero of the DreamWorks animated films?
explanation: Shrek is the hero of the 2001 animated film of the same name.

q: In which sport do players perform a «slam dunk»?
explanation: A slam dunk is a powerful shot from above into the basket.

q: Which country is regarded as the birthplace of pizza?
explanation: Modern pizza comes from Naples, Italy.

q: What is measured with a thermometer?
explanation: A thermometer measures temperature.

q: What does the abbreviation «PC» usually stand for?
explanation: PC stands for personal computer.

q: What is the force that pulls objects towards the Earth called?
explanation: Gravity is the force of attraction.

q: On which continent is Brazil?
explanation: Brazil is the largest country of South America.

q: What is the profession of a person who treats animals?
explanation: A veterinarian treats animals.

q: In which country did the ancient Olympic Games originate?
explanation: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece.

q: Which is the largest animal on Earth?
explanation: The blue whale is the largest known animal.

q: What is the chemical symbol of gold?
explanation: Au comes from the Latin aurum.

q: Which city is the capital of Canada?
explanation: Canada's capital is Ottawa, not the largest city, Toronto.

q: In which year did the First World War begin?
explanation: The war began in the summer of 1914.

q: Who wrote the novel «Pride and Prejudice»?
explanation: The novel was published in 1813.

q: Which artist painted «The Scream»?
explanation: «The Scream» is the best-known work of the Norwegian Edvard Munch.

q: In which country was the band The Beatles formed?
explanation: The Beatles were formed in Liverpool, England.

q: Who directed both «Jaws» and «Schindler's List»?
explanation: Both films were directed by Steven Spielberg.

q: In which country were the 2016 Summer Olympic Games held?
explanation: The 2016 Games were hosted by Rio de Janeiro.

q: Which spice is generally considered the most expensive in the world by weight?
explanation: Saffron is harvested by hand from crocus flowers.

q: Which substance in the blood carries oxygen?
explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds oxygen.

q: Who co-founded Microsoft together with Paul Allen?
explanation: Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in 1975.

q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
explanation: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers.

q: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
explanation: The five are the US, Russia, China, the UK and France.

q: Which planet is best known for its bright rings?
explanation: Saturn's rings are visible even through a small telescope.

q: Which mountain is the highest above sea level?
explanation: Everest rises to about 8,849 m above sea level.

q: Who led the 1492 voyage that brought Europeans to the Americas?
explanation: Columbus landed in the Caribbean in 1492.

q: How many degrees are there in a right angle?
explanation: A right angle is 90 degrees.

q: Who wrote the novel «Les Misérables»?
explanation: «Les Misérables» was published by Victor Hugo in 1862.

q: In which city is the Prado Museum?
explanation: The Prado is the main art museum of Madrid.

q: Who composed the opera «The Magic Flute»?
explanation: Mozart composed it in 1791.

q: Which studio made «Toy Story», the first full-length computer-animated film?
explanation: «Toy Story» (1995) was made by Pixar.

q: How many players of one team are on the court at once in volleyball?
explanation: Volleyball is played six a side.

q: What is the traditional Japanese drink sake made from?
explanation: Sake is a rice-based drink.

q: Which is the largest human organ by surface area?
explanation: The skin is the largest organ by surface area.

q: What does the abbreviation USB stand for?
explanation: USB is short for Universal Serial Bus.

q: Which gas makes up most of the Earth's atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere.

q: The outline of which European country is often compared to a boot?
explanation: The Italian peninsula looks like a boot.

q: What is the currency of Japan called?
explanation: Japan's currency is the yen.

q: Which civilisation built the city of Machu Picchu?
explanation: The Incas built Machu Picchu in the Andes in the 15th century.

q: What is the largest hot desert in the world called?
explanation: The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth.
